target.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane
target.body:
Related: #72015 (this addresses the recall-lane serialization portion of that report; the QMD boot-initialization portion is separate)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and test update were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where, on multi-agent gateways, memory recall runs from different agents queue behind each other. The active-memory recall subagent always enqueues on the single shared `active-memory` lane, and command lanes default to `maxConcurrent: 1`, so every agent's recall serializes globally. The lane wait burns the recall's turn-scoped time budget, so under concurrent traffic (several agents active at once, or a burst of session resets) recalls run late, time out, or are skipped, and users see replies without memory context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Key the recall lane by agent id (`active-memory:<agentId>`) so recalls serialize per agent instead of across the whole gateway. Lanes are created lazily on first use, so no lane registration change is needed. `agentId` is already a required parameter at the enqueue site. Single-agent deployments behave exactly as before (one agent, one lane).

## User Impact

On multi-agent gateways, one agent's memory recall no longer delays every other agent's. Recall latency under concurrent load drops and fewer recall time budgets are exhausted while queued, so memory injection lands more reliably. No configuration change; single-agent installs see no behavioral difference.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-active-memory.config.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts` passes 154/154, including the updated lane assertion (agent `main` now enqueues on `active-memory:main`).
- Live observation motivating the fix: on a multi-agent gateway, recall queue-wait clusters coincided with degraded or skipped memory injection whenever several agents were active in the same window; single-agent sessions on the same build were unaffected.
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).
